source.title: It's All Training: A Fully Synthetic Single-Stage Recipe for LLMs
source.authors: Pierre-Carl Langlais; Pieter Delobelle; Yannick Detrois; Pavel Chizhov; C. Rosas Hinostroza; Neil Si Smail; Benjamin Burtin; Hanna Shcharbakova; Ivan P. Yamshchikov; A. Stasenko

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a preliminary comparison of scaling-law fits across training-data sources and argues that engineered data can shift the loss curve. It does not test the broader parameter, token, compute, or compute-optimal laws.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the text's statement that preliminary scaling-law fits on iso-compute 600M runs show a lower asymptotic loss floor for SYNTH than for FineWiki and FinePDFs-Edu. The paper says losses are not directly comparable across corpora. Final cross-entropies and the statement that loss was still decreasing are not held-out losses, so they are not rows for these claim versions. Downstream benchmark comparisons and cited scaling-law results do not report tests of the versions here.
record.test_reason: The only scaling-law result is a preliminary, unquantified comparison of fits on three iso-compute 600M runs. It reports a lower asymptotic loss floor on SYNTH than on FineWiki and FinePDFs-Edu. The authors say loss 'is not directly comparable across corpora', so a floor difference across different training and evaluation distributions cannot show the setup-dependence V7 names, which is exponents or the compute-optimal split. No exponents, coefficients, held-out losses or allocations are reported. The conclusion's claim that Chinchilla coefficients do not describe engineered data is an argument, not a measured test.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors argue that Chinchilla coefficients were fit on web text, and that engineered data 'shifts the curve' with training productive past the 20x ratio. They treat data quality as a controllable axis alongside size and tokens. They themselves label the scaling-fit comparison preliminary and say losses are not comparable across corpora. The conclusion rests on that unquantified comparison and on downstream results, not on reported fit coefficients.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives a preliminary data-source comparison of scaling-law fits on iso-compute 600M runs, rather than a broad parameter/token/compute scaling sweep or a compute-optimal allocation analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that training-data source changes the fitted asymptotic loss floor; it does not report sensitivity to other fitting choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Preliminary scaling-law fits on three iso-compute 600M runs show a lower asymptotic loss floor for SYNTH than for FineWiki and FinePDFs-Edu. No values are given, and the authors caution that losses are not comparable across corpora.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The irreducible-loss term of a fitted scaling law differs with the pretraining corpus (data entropy or learnability).

fits_no_version.finding: A 600M model trained at 264x tokens per parameter (158B tokens) still had decreasing training loss at step 151,000, with no spikes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training loss keeps falling well beyond the Chinchilla-optimal token-to-parameter ratio on engineered synthetic data.

record.problems: The scaling-fit result is described as preliminary, with no fit coefficients, exact loss-floor values, or uncertainty reported. The authors caution that losses are not directly comparable across corpora. The comparison is limited to 600M runs and does not test held-out loss laws or compute-optimal allocation.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were eligible for these claim versions. The reported final cross-entropies are not identified as held-out losses; downstream evaluations do not establish downstream predictability from scale or pretraining loss.

untested.parts: No power law in parameters, tokens or compute on held-out loss; only final training cross-entropies (1.52, 1.15, 1.19) are reported.
No extrapolation from small to large runs.
No compute-optimal allocation fitted. The Chinchilla 20x ratio is cited, and the 600M model was trained at 264x with training loss still falling; this does not measure the optimum.
Depth ablations and an architecture-ablation sweep are mentioned (Infrastructure; checklist item 8) but no loss results are reported.
Synthetic text pretraining only; no power-law form tested in another modality or regime.
Downstream benchmarks are compared across models and corpora, not as a function of scale or loss.
No fitted exponents, compute-optimal splits, or effects of parameter counting, schedule or fitting method; only an unquantified asymptotic-floor difference across non-comparable corpora.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V7 'supports' label is dropped: the measure (asymptotic floor across corpora with different loss scales) cannot show exponent or allocation dependence, and no numbers are reported. The MoE matching the dense model's final cross-entropy (1.19) on about 32% of tokens is training loss and a cross-architecture comparison, not a scaling test. The architecture-ablation sweep (10B tokens per configuration) is mentioned without results and could bear on V4 if released.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining-loss power law is tested across parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fits are used to predict much larger runs.
No compute-optimal parameter/token allocation or its trend with compute is tested.
The text mentions architecture exploration but does not report a fixed-parameter comparison of architecture effects on loss.
Synthetic text pretraining is used, but the paper does not test whether the same power-law form holds across modalities or training regimes.
Downstream tasks are evaluated, but the paper does not test their predictability from scale or pretraining loss.

The paper reports a data-source-related difference in fitted asymptotic loss, but does not report fitted exponents, compute-optimal allocations, effects of parameter counting or fitting method, or systematic curve bending.

rows.subject: BAGUETTOTRON-600M
rows.operation_detail: Compared preliminary scaling-law fits for iso-compute runs across training-data sources.

conditions.value: SYNTH compared with FineWiki and FinePDFs-Edu

rows.measure: Asymptotic cross-entropy loss floor from scaling-law fits
rows.baseline: FineWiki and FinePDFs-Edu scraped-data runs; exact loss floors not stated
rows.value: SYNTH has a lower asymptotic loss floor; exact value not stated
rows.note: Reported as preliminary. The authors caution that loss is not directly comparable across corpora; FineWiki reaches its low loss after approximately 17 epochs over approximately 9B tokens.
rows.check: V7 concerns fitted exponents and the compute-optimal split depending on setup. R1 compares only the asymptotic (irreducible) loss floor across corpora whose losses the authors say are not comparable. No floor values, exponents or uncertainty are given. The floor reflects each corpus's own entropy, so the measure cannot show V7's effect. The 'observed' state and V7 link are not justified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
